docs.title: Wealth Pilot Documentation 🧭
docs.text:
Strategic Wealth & Asset Allocation Guidance Platform

Welcome to the documentation for Wealth Pilot, an open-source, local-first platform designed for mid-to-long term wealth planning, strategic asset allocation, and actionable financial guidance.

docs.title: Why Wealth Pilot?
docs.text:
Most personal finance apps fall into one of two extremes: 1. Micro-Budgeting Apps (e.g. YNAB, Monarch): Focus on categorizing every €3 coffee and managing envelope budgets. They offer little to no strategic investment guidance. 2. Passive Net Worth Dashboards (e.g. Kubera, Finary): Provide high-level aggregation across accounts, but lack proactive advice on how to rebalance, which debts to pay off, or where to deploy monthly surplus cashflow.

Wealth Pilot bridges this gap: - Macro Allocation Buckets: Organize assets into target pillars (e.g. Core World ETFs, High-Conviction Growth, Gold/Commodities, Cash Buffers, Real Estate) with customizable drift tolerances. - Unified Balance Sheet: Connects investment accounts (PDT MCP), bank checking cashflow (KBC CSV), savings accounts (Bunq), and active debts (mortgages, credit lines). - Proactive Guidance Engine: Rebalances portfolios using incoming monthly cash deposits (Buy-Only Rebalancing) without forcing taxable asset sales or broker fees. - Debt vs. Investing Optimization: Evaluates debt APR against long-term expected portfolio returns (Avalanche vs Snowball). - AI Financial Advisor: Pluggable LLM interface (BYO API key) delivering personalized strategic commentary. - Privacy & Zero Vendor Lock-in: 100% local execution with zero cloud telemetry.

docs.title: Architectural Highlights
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot strictly implements Uncle Bob's Clean Architecture:

  • domain/: Pure business models (Money, Asset, Liability, Bucket, AllocationRule, BalanceSheet). Zero third-party dependencies.
  • use_cases/: Application business rules (CalculateBucketAllocation, AdviseContribution, AdviseDebtPayoff, ProjectNetWorth, CategorizeTransactions, OptimizeTax).
  • adapters/: Ingestion gateways (KBC CSV, PDT MCP, Generic CSV/YAML) and repositories.
  • delivery/: Modern local FastAPI web dashboard with PWA support, alongside a scriptable CLI.

docs.title: Getting Started with Wealth Pilot
docs.text: Follow this guide to get Wealth Pilot running locally in minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • uv (Modern high-performance Python package manager)
# Install uv if you don't already have it
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/tiwu/wealth-pilot.git
cd wealth-pilot

# Sync dependencies into local virtual environment
uv sync --extra dev

docs.title: 1. Interactive Web Dashboard (Recommended)
docs.text:
Launch the local web dashboard:

uv run wealth-pilot web

Open your browser at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

  • Mobile / PWA: On iOS (Safari) or Android (Chrome), tap Share -> Add to Home Screen to install Wealth Pilot as a standalone mobile application.

docs.title: 2. Scriptable CLI Commands
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot includes a rich terminal CLI for quick checks:

# View consolidated Balance Sheet, Net Worth, and Bucket status
uv run wealth-pilot status

# Calculate smart buy-only allocation advice for a monthly deposit
uv run wealth-pilot advise --deposit 1500

# Parse and inspect a bank statement or portfolio CSV
uv run wealth-pilot ingest path/to/kbc-export.csv

# Generate a sample generic CSV template
uv run wealth-pilot template --output template.csv

docs.title: Initial Configuration
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot automatically initializes default strategic buckets and configuration in ~/.wealth_pilot/portfolio.yaml.

You can customize: - Bucket names, target weights (%), and drift tolerances (±%). - Manual accounts (e.g. Bunq savings balance, unlisted property value). - Active debts (mortgage principal balances, interest rate APRs).

docs.title: AI Financial Advisor Setup
docs.text: Wealth Pilot includes an optional AI Financial Advisor layer designed to provide qualitative, human-readable reviews of your macro financial plan.

docs.title: Bring Your Own API Key (BYO Key)
docs.text:
To guarantee complete privacy and zero markups, you provide your own API key from your preferred provider:

  1. Google Gemini (Recommended): Free or pay-as-you-go via Google AI Studio.
  2. OpenAI: GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini via platform.openai.com.
  3. Anthropic: Claude 3.5 Haiku / Sonnet via console.anthropic.com.
  4. Local Ollama: 100% offline local inference (no API key required).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
You can enter your API key directly in the Web Dashboard under the 🤖 AI Advisor tab, or export it in your environment:

# Example environment variables
export GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-key"
# or
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-key"

docs.title: Privacy Protection
docs.text: When an AI review is requested, Wealth Pilot: - Never transmits your account numbers, bank identifiers, counterparty names, or personal identities. - Sends only high-level aggregated metrics: total assets, total debt, debt APRs, bucket percentage deviations, and monthly cashflow surplus.

docs.title: Balance Sheet & Net Worth Overview
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot tracks both sides of your personal ledger to compute true economic net worth:

$$\text{Net Worth} = \text{Total Assets} - \text{Total Liabilities}$$

docs.title: 1. Assets
docs.text:
• Liquid Cash & Checking: Current account balance from your bank statement (e.g. KBC).
  • High-Yield Savings: Emergency cash reserves (e.g. Bunq).
  • Investment Portfolio: Brokerage positions (PDT MCP, Saxo, DEGIRO, Bolero).
  • Real Estate / Equity: Estimated property values.

docs.title: 2. Liabilities (Debts)
docs.text:
• Mortgages (Woningkrediet): Long-term fixed or variable real estate loans.
  • Consumer Credit (Flex Budget): Revolving lines of credit or car loans.
  • Student Loans / Margin Debt: Discretionary borrowing.

docs.title: 3. Monthly Cashflow & Surplus
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot computes your Monthly Free Cashflow:

$$\text{Monthly Free Cashflow} = \text{Net Income} - (\text{Fixed Costs} + \text{Debt Servicing} + \text{Living Expenses})$$

This surplus represents your investable capacity—the engine that drives your buy-only rebalancing and wealth compounding.

docs.title: Strategic Allocation Buckets
docs.text: Wealth Pilot organizes all your financial holdings into macro strategic allocation buckets.

docs.title: What is a Bucket?
docs.text:
A Bucket represents a strategic investment pillar or wealth goal, rather than an arbitrary financial product.

Common examples: - Core World ETFs (e.g. 50%): Broad, low-cost global equity index funds (e.g. VWCE, IWDA). - High-Conviction Tech / Equities (e.g. 35%): Individual stock positions (e.g. AAPL, NVDA) with higher growth potential. - Gold & Commodities (e.g. 5%): Inflation hedges and uncorrelated assets. - Liquid Emergency Buffer (e.g. 10%): High-yield cash reserves in checking/savings (KBC, Bunq).

docs.title: Target Weight & Drift Tolerance
docs.text: Each bucket is defined by: 1. Target Weight (%): The ideal percentage of your total liquid portfolio value. 2. Drift Tolerance (±%): The acceptable deviation band before a rebalance alert is triggered (default: ±3.0%).

docs.title: Drift Statuses:
docs.text:
• BALANCED (🟢): Current weight is within the target weight ± drift tolerance.
  • UNDERWEIGHT (🔵): Current weight is below target by more than the tolerance. Cash deposits will be routed here.
  • OVERWEIGHT (🟡): Current weight exceeds target by more than tolerance.

docs.title: Rule-Based Asset Matching
docs.text: Assets are dynamically assigned to buckets using declarative rules: - Symbols: Match specific tickers (e.g. AAPL, VWCE). - ISINs: Match exact security identifiers (e.g. NL0010273215, IE00BK5BQT80). - Asset Classes: Match entire classes (EQUITY, ETF, COMMODITY, CRYPTO, CASH). - Institutions: Match specific accounts (e.g. KBC, Bunq).

docs.title: Buy-Only Rebalancing Strategy
docs.text:
Traditional portfolio rebalancing involves selling over-allocated winners and buying under-allocated laggards. While mathematically sound, selling in the real world introduces friction:

  1. Transaction Fees & Spreads: Broker commissions on both sell orders and buy orders.
  2. Transaction Taxes (TOB): E.g., Belgian stock exchange tax on both sales and purchases.
  3. Capital Gains Taxes: Realizing taxable profits unnecessarily.

docs.title: The Buy-Only Cash Injection Model
docs.text:
Wealth Pilot defaults to Buy-Only Rebalancing:

  1. You specify an incoming cash deposit (e.g. your monthly savings of €1,500).
  2. The engine identifies which buckets are currently UNDERWEIGHT (where Current Weight < Target Weight).
  3. The deposit is distributed proportionally to each bucket's deficit, bringing the overall portfolio toward target weights with zero forced sales.
Example:
Planned Deposit: € 2,000.00
- Core World ETF Deficit: € 15,000 (60% of total shortfall) -> BUY € 1,200.00
- Tech Conviction Deficit: € 10,000 (40% of total shortfall) -> BUY € 800.00
- Gold Bucket: Already balanced -> BUY € 0.00

By accumulating new cash directly into underweight assets, you rebalance continuously without selling your winners.

docs.title: Debt Payoff Strategy: Avalanche vs. Investing
docs.text:
A fundamental dilemma for wealth builders with surplus cashflow is: "Should I pay down my debts faster, or invest the money in my portfolio?"

Wealth Pilot uses a mathematical framework to resolve this trade-off.

docs.title: The Hurdle Rate Framework
docs.text: Wealth Pilot compares each liability's Annual Percentage Rate (APR) against your expected long-term portfolio compound annual growth rate (CAGR, default: 7.0%):

docs.title: 1. High-Interest Debt (APR > 5.0%) -> Accelerate Payoff (Debt Avalanche)
docs.text:
• Examples: Consumer lines of credit (Flex Budget), car loans, credit cards.
  • Why: Paying off a 9.5% loan provides a guaranteed, risk-free return of 9.5%. No equity market can guarantee that return.
  • Priority: Direct all surplus monthly cashflow toward extinguishing this debt first.

docs.title: 2. Low-Interest Debt (APR < 3.0%) -> Maintain Minimums & Invest
docs.text:
• Examples: Fixed-rate mortgages (Woningkrediet at 1.5% - 2.5%).
  • Why: When borrowing costs are 1.85% and expected equity compounding is 7.0%, the expected net wealth accumulation is significantly higher by investing the surplus in productive assets rather than prepaying the mortgage.
  • Priority: Maintain required contractual monthly payments and invest the remaining surplus into underweight buckets.

docs.title: Net Worth Milestone Projections
docs.text: Wealth Pilot models compound wealth growth over 5, 10, 20, and 30 years using multi-variable trajectory simulations.

docs.title: Compounding Variables
docs.text:
1. Current Net Worth: Starting assets minus active liabilities.
  2. Monthly Savings Rate: Net investable cashflow surplus derived from your bank statement and income.
  3. Compound Annual Return (CAGR): Long-term portfolio return assumption (default: 7.0%).
  4. Debt Amortization: Gradual paydown of principal balances over the loan lifecycle.

docs.title: Wealth Milestones
docs.text: The projection engine tracks when your net worth trajectory crosses key financial milestones: - €100k: The critical baseline where investment returns begin noticeably accelerating savings. - €250k: Quarter-million milestone. - €500k: Half-million milestone. - €1M: Liquid millionaire milestone. - Financial Independence (FI): The crossover point where annual investment yield exceeds estimated annual living expenses (using the 4.0% safe withdrawal rule).

docs.title: Belgian Capital Gains Tax Optimization
docs.text: For Belgian tax residents, capital gains legislation includes specific transitional rules and exemption limits.

docs.title: Key Fiscal Parameters
docs.text:
1. Reference Benchmark Price (Dec 31, 2025):
  2. For long-held shares, the fiscal cost basis is benchmarked to the closing market price on December 31, 2025.
  3. Only capital appreciation above this reference price is subject to taxation upon sale.
  4. Annual Capital Gains Exemption (€10,000.00):
  5. Belgian tax residents benefit from a €10,000 annual exemption on realized capital gains.
  6. Realized gains within the €10,000 limit incur 0% tax.
  7. Tax Rate Above Exemption (10.0%):
  8. Any realized net gain exceeding €10,000 in a calendar year is taxed at 10%.

docs.title: Guidance Engine Integration
docs.text: When you review your rebalancing options: - Wealth Pilot calculates your current taxable gain per share against the benchmark price. - It calculates how many shares can be sold without exceeding the €10,000 exemption. - If rebalancing requires selling over-allocated shares, it alerts you if the sale would trigger the 10% tax.

docs.title: Generic CSV / Excel Ingestion
docs.text: For brokerages or banks that do not have an automated connector, Wealth Pilot provides an open, standard CSV format.

docs.title: CSV Column Headers
docs.text: name,symbol,isin,asset_class,shares,current_price,current_value,institution,currency

docs.title: Supported Columns:
docs.text:
• name: Security or account name (e.g. Microsoft Corp.)
  • symbol: Ticker symbol (e.g. MSFT, VWCE)
  • isin: 12-character ISIN code (e.g. US5949181045)
  • asset_class: EQUITY, ETF, COMMODITY, CRYPTO, CASH, or REAL_ESTATE
  • shares: Number of units held
  • current_price: Market price per share
  • current_value: Total valuation in the specified currency
  • institution: Brokerage or bank name (e.g. DEGIRO, Saxo Bank, Bolero)
  • currency: Currency code (default: EUR)

docs.title: Generating a Sample Template
docs.text:
You can generate a sample CSV directly from the CLI or download it from the Web Dashboard:

uv run wealth-pilot template --output portfolio_template.csv

docs.title: Ingesting Belgian KBC Bank Statements
docs.text: Wealth Pilot features native, zero-configuration support for KBC Bank CSV statement exports.

docs.title: How to Export from KBC Touch / KBC Mobile
docs.text:
1. Log in to KBC Touch (web) or KBC Mobile.
  2. Navigate to your checking account (Zichtrekening).
  3. Click Historiek exporteren (Export History) -> Select CSV-formaat.
  4. Download the .csv file.

docs.title: File Format Specs Handled Automatically
docs.text:
• Encoding: ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) / Windows-1252
  • Delimiter: Semicolon (;)
  • Number Formats: European format (e.g., -579,68 or 1.452,04)
  • Date Format: DD/MM/YYYY

docs.title: Automated Discovery
docs.text: When you upload or ingest your KBC CSV: 1. Liquid Checking Balance: Extracted from the most recent transaction's Saldo column and assigned to the Cash asset. 2. Liabilities Discovery: Scans descriptions for loan references (WONINGKREDIET and FLEX BUDGET) and automatically records active debts. 3. Monthly Debt Servicing: Sums recurring mortgage repayments and consumer credit payments. 4. Income Extraction: Averages recurring salary deposits from your employer. 5. Interactive Re-Bucketing: Displays all transactions in the Web Dashboard, allowing you to re-bucket any transaction and save custom categorization rules.

docs.title: Manual Accounts & Bunq Integration
docs.text: Certain financial assets and liabilities don't require automated feeds or CSV statements to track accurately. Wealth Pilot allows you to define these directly in your portfolio.yaml or through the Web UI.

docs.title: Configuring Bunq Savings
docs.text:
For accounts like Bunq High-Yield Savings where you maintain an emergency reserve:

manual_assets:
  - id: "bunq-savings"
    name: "Bunq High-Yield Savings"
    symbol: "SAVINGS"
    asset_class: "CASH"
    current_value: 15000.00
    institution: "Bunq"
    currency: "EUR"

docs.title: Configuring Real Estate & Mortgages
docs.text:
To model primary residence equity alongside mortgages:

manual_assets:
  - id: "primary-home"
    name: "Primary Residence (Estimated Market Value)"
    asset_class: "REAL_ESTATE"
    current_value: 420000.00
    institution: "Private Property"

manual_liabilities:
  - id: "mortgage-woningkrediet-1"
    name: "KBC Woningkrediet (Fixed Rate)"
    loan_type: "MORTGAGE"
    principal_balance: 140000.00
    interest_rate_pct: 1.85
    monthly_payment: 579.68
    institution: "KBC"

docs.title: PDT MCP Server Integration
docs.text: Wealth Pilot connects directly to the Portfolio Dividend Tracker (PDT) MCP server over JSON-RPC.

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
1. The PdtMcpGateway queries the PDT MCP server tools:
  2. pdt-get-portfolio: Returns aggregate net invested, current worth, and cash.
  3. pdt-get-portfolio-holdings: Returns open positions, live prices, quantities, and cost basis.
  4. pdt-list-x-ray-holdings: Provides look-through breakdown into underlying ETF holdings.
  5. The responses are automatically converted into unified domain Asset entities.
  6. Assets are mapped into your configured Strategic Buckets by ticker, ISIN, or asset class.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
In ~/.wealth_pilot/portfolio.yaml or environment variables:

pdt_mcp:
  url: "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
  auth_token: "your-pdt-token"
